scenes.headline: How a model that cannot write runs an agent loop
scenes.sub: switch lists the actions in code; the model picks one
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Detent! A decision model cannot write a tool call. This framework writes them in code instead.

scenes.text: Your code lists the legal actions and labels them. The model only scores the labels, so it can never invent an action.
scenes.say: Your code lists the legal actions. The model only scores the labels, so it can never invent an action.

steps.say: The question function reads the state and lists the legal actions as labels.
The model sees the labels and nothing else to choose from.
Code checks the label is on the menu, then the transition runs the action.
Every state and answer goes in the trace, so a run can be replayed without the model.

left.title: Chat-model agent
items: The model writes the tool call as text
The harness parses and validates it
left.say: In a chat agent the model writes the tool call, and the harness must parse it.

right.title: switch
items: The model only picks a label
right.say: Here code writes every action first, and the model picks a label.

scenes.title: Request size per step on my toy run
scenes.say: On my toy run a request grew from one hundred thirty-two to three hundred forty-seven tokens as the view filled with logs, then fell to three hundred fourteen.

scenes.label: Bad deciders that ended a run as failed
scenes.say: I ran eleven bad deciders. Six ended the run failed with a named reason. One too-long request recovered.

scenes.text: Use it for a finite menu repeated over a state. If the model must write something, it does not fit.

scenes.say: Code lists the actions, the model picks a label, and a bad label stops the run.
